title: Project Jupiter passes 25% mark in Doña Ana County
source_used: Albuquerque Journal opinion column by Bob Clark, a Clayco executive (pool link, fetched text; author from the page's structured data)
key_facts: The column is an opinion piece by Bob Clark, an executive at the construction firm Clayco, which is building Project Jupiter with Kiewit New Mexico Co., Oracle, STACK Infrastructure and local and union workers.

Clayco and Kiewit placed the final structural beam atop the 855,000-square-foot first portion of the campus, completing its primary structural framework; the column says the project is now more than 25% complete.

It says the project is on pace to create more than 7,000 construction jobs and 1,500 ongoing jobs, and that nearly 1,000 New Mexico residents, 466 of them from Doña Ana County, have worked on it so far.
It says more than 3,600 workers have completed more than 2.8 million labor hours, including more than 900 union members.
It says the campus will use closed-loop, non-evaporative cooling and that its cooling systems and fuel cells will not use community drinking water.
It promises a public dashboard, once the campus is live, on noise, water use, heat, light and emissions.
The column does not mention the power-supply delays reported in September, when Oracle sent a force majeure notice over delayed power for the project (our 25 and 27 Sep 2026 editions).
quote_evidence: We recently marked a major milestone: Clayco and Kiewit placed the final structural beam atop the 855,000-square-foot first portion of the campus, completing its primary structural framework.
This means Project Jupiter is now more than 25% complete.
Project Jupiter will use closed-loop, non-evaporative cooling that continuously reuses liquid in sealed systems, and its cooling systems and fuel cells will not use community drinking water.
why_it_matters_hint: A progress report and promises on jobs and water from the builder itself, with no independent check, on a campus whose power supply was reported delayed in September.
event_date: Column published 5 Oct 2026; the beam-placing milestone is described as recent and is not dated.
notes: An opinion column written by the builder, so every figure is a company claim. A column titled 'Building Project Jupiter for southern New Mexico' ran in the Las Cruces Sun-News opinion section on 3 Oct 2026 (page not readable here, so it is not confirmed to be the same text). The milestone is not dated.
